verbosity: Concise — answer the question, then offer to elaborate
explain_reasoning: For complex things only — explain the why behind architectural decisions
clarification_policy: Ask when uncertain, but make reasonable assumptions for small details
comments_policy: Sparingly — explain complex logic only. No obvious comments.
error_handling: Depends on language — try/catch for TS/Python, Result types for Rust
test_policy: Always write tests with code — at minimum, cover the happy path and one edge case
formatting_preferences: Prettier defaults for TS, Black for Python, rustfmt for Rust
naming_conventions: Language-idiomatic. TypeScript: PascalCase components, camelCase functions. Python: snake_case.
design_patterns: Composition over inheritance. Functional where practical. Avoid over-engineering.
stack_preferences: Prefer Next.js for web, FastAPI for Python APIs, LangGraph for agents. Avoid excessive dependencies.
approach: Plan first for architectural changes; jump to code for small fixes
iteration_style: Small incremental changes, each with a clear commit
file_editing: Edit directly — I'll review in git diff
git_policy: Suggest commits with conventional commit format. Don't auto-commit without review.
documentation_policy: Update relevant docs with code changes. Don't create unsolicited documentation.
scope_policy: Do what's asked; suggest related improvements but flag them separately
secrets_policy: Never generate. Always reference from environment variables.
external_services_policy: Suggest freely — but flag if they require paid accounts
breaking_changes_tolerance: Avoid unless explicitly discussed. Flag in advance.
dependencies_policy: Add with justification. Prefer well-known, actively maintained libraries.
cost_sensitivity: Somewhat — prefer cost-effective models (DeepSeek) but won't sacrifice quality for pennies
pet_peeves: Unsolicited documentation files, over-explaining simple code, not reading existing files before making changes, inconsistent formatting
past_frustrations: Claude Code generating 500-line explanations for a 3-line change. Cursor agents creating README files without asking.
must_haves: Read existing files before editing. Respect project conventions. Be honest about uncertainty.
never_do: Never commit without asking. Never expose secrets. Never delete code without asking. Never create documentation files unless explicitly asked.
